title: Deploy backfill safety-net for partial-hour credit offsets to improve invoice accuracy
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Context: We have recurring customer reports and a handful of recent investigations where rate-limit credits and partial-hour quota adjustments created negative or duplicate invoice lines after the export job ran during busy retry windows. Root cause patterns include: (1) late-arriving meter pulses from retry storms, (2) mid-hour plan switches that change proration logic, and (3) concurrent credit application + hourly-aggregation races. Goals: 1) eliminate duplicate/negative invoice lines caused by late credit backfills, 2) make export idempotent and retry-safe with deterministic signatures, 3) provide an automated 'safety-net' backfill job that quarantines ambiguous adjustments and only exports reconciled, watermarked offsets. This ticket implements the safety-net job, telemetry, and rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Nightly backfill safety-net job runs and produces idempotent candidate export lines per tenant without modifying live invoice lines (shadow mode)
Safety-net applies tenant-level watermarking: once an export for a timestamp is accepted, subsequent late pulses are either merged deterministically or routed to a quarantine review queue
Export lines include deterministic fingerprints (export_signature) so downstream consumers (Stripe/Netsuite) can dedupe on ingest
Automated reconciliation dashboard (Looker) shows reduction in duplicate/negative invoice lines in a 2-week shadow run vs baseline

Rollout plan executed: shadow (2 weeks) -> opt-in beta tenants (low volume) -> full enable with fallback toggle; no more than 0.5% increase in export latency and no customer-visible invoice drift after full enablement
implementation_notes: Create new service job billing-backfill-safetynet running in k8s CronJob (daily 03:00 UTC) and a one-off run for backfill window
Add tenant_watermark table (tenant_id, last_exported_event_ts, last_export_signature) used by job to decide idempotency; ensure table writes are idempotent and transactionally updated

Algorithm: 1) collect late meter events since last_exported_event_ts up to sentinel (now - 2m), 2) compute canonical offsets grouped by (tenant, sku, hour_bucket), 3) compute export_signature = sha256(tenant|hour|sku|sum_tokens|timestamp_bucket) and compare with last_export_signature, 4) if mismatch route to quarantine; otherwise include in candidate export
Inject export_signature into export line metadata and Stripe metadata (metadata["export_signature"]) for downstream idempotency
Quarantine queue stored in DynamoDB with TTL and human-review link; include auto-escalation rule after 3 failed reconciliations
Shadow mode: job writes candidate exports to namespace 'shadow_exports' and updates dashboards but does not post to Stripe/Netsuite until opt-in
Performance: batch aggregation implemented in CTE SQL + streaming mapreduce to avoid O(n^2) in memory for large tenants; ensure discovery and backpressure if tenant event volume > 10M rows / day
Add metrics: backfill.job.runs, backfill.processed_tenants, backfill.quarantined_lines, backfill.duplicate_signatures, export.signature_collision_rate
Add alerts: >=1% quarantined lines for >1 hour => pager to oncall billing-eng; signature collision rate >0.01% for >1 hour => paging and automatic rollback
qa_plan: Stage run: seed staging with synthetic late pulses for 10 tenants and verify shadow_exports contain expected deterministic signatures
End-to-end test: run nightly job in staging, then run an idempotent re-export to a Stripe sandbox and assert no duplicate invoice lines are created
Regression tests: add unit tests for export_signature function with edge cases (floating rounding, timezone boundaries, DST transitions), and integration test for tenant_watermark update concurrency
Load test: synthetic run for one high-volume tenant (~15M events/day) to validate memory and batch behavior
Manual verification checklist for opt-in tenants: compare pre/post exports in Looker and confirm invoice balances unchanged after 7 days
risks: Incorrect signature logic could cause legitimate adjustments to be suppressed — mitigated by shadow runs and quarantine review
High-volume tenants could cause backfill job to exceed memory/time budgets — mitigated by paginated aggregation and per-tenant throttling
Adding metadata to Stripe export may increase per-line payload size — validated with Stripe sandbox tests
Changing export semantics risks downstream Netsuite mappings — include mapping compatibility tests and a rollback path that preserves prior export format
comments: 2026-01-21 - Asha Kapoor: Investigated multiple customer reports; tied to retry storms during DST boundary. Drafted design and estimation. Listed as P1 because invoice integrity impacts finance and customers.

2026-01-28 - Liam Chen: Spike complete. Verified deterministic signature approach locally. Found one edge case where fractional token rounding caused signature mismatch. Decided to canonicalize token sums to integer microtokens before hashing.
2026-02-04 - Diego Martinez (finance): Reviewed acceptance criteria. Requested explicit test showing zero net change to invoice totals in shadow runs for at least 2 weeks before opt-in.
2026-02-15 - Incident postmortem linked; added quarantine requirement to avoid auto-applying ambiguous offsets seen in the INC-2026-02-15 incident.
2026-02-25 - PR opened: billing: add backfill job scaffolding (PR#2487). Needs data-model review and migration plan for tenant_watermark table.
2026-03-02 - Eleanor Shaw (SRE): Reviewed CronJob resource requests. Suggests k8s HPA not required; prefer per-tenant pagination to avoid OOMs. Added runbook for manual quarantine review.

2026-03-10 - Liam Chen: Shadow run started for 50 low-volume tenants. Early telemetry: backfill.processed_tenants=50, backfill.quarantined_lines=12 (mostly DST-related edge cases). No duplicate invoices observed in Stripe sandbox. Proceeding to 2-week shadow window.
